data.what_done: Reviewed Task tool and command/subtask flows to trace how subagent model selection and agent routing behave.
data.approach_taken: Searched the repo for Task tool implementation, agent config handling, and command/subtask creation paths; cross-referenced model selection logic and defaults.
data.challenges_faced: Isolating why a primary agent can appear in Task calls required tracing both direct Task tool usage and the command-generated subtask path.
data.how_solved: Mapped Task tool execution and the command subtask condition, then identified fallback and missing mode enforcement in the Task tool.
data.reasoning: Task tool falls back to the parent message model when the subagent lacks a model and does not enforce subagent-only usage; commands with subtask=true can therefore trigger Task calls using the current primary agent/model.
next_steps: Decide whether to enforce subagent-only validation in TaskTool (reject primary agents).
Audit commands with subtask:true and set command.agent to a dedicated subagent or flip subtask:false.
